### Coulomb1785Electricity
- **Authors**: Charles-Augustin Coulomb ("M. Coulomb"). **Title**: Premier mémoire sur l'électricité et le magnétisme. **Journal**: Histoire de l'Académie Royale des Sciences, Année 1785, avec les Mémoires de Mathématique & de Physique pour la même année (Mémoires section), pp. 569-577. Paris, Imprimerie Royale, printed 1788. No DOI.
- **Claim supported**: "Electromagnetism can be compared with the same floor. Coulomb's law \citep{Coulomb1785Electricity} divided by the floor force is $e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2)/F_1(r)=e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0\hbar c)$" (sgm_core_rewrite.tex L2024, eq:alpha_crossing). The citation is for the inverse-square law of the electric force.
- **Source URL**: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k35847 (BnF Gallica scan of the Année 1785 volume). Pages read as images through the Gallica IIIF service: title page = view f1; p. 569 = f759; p. 572 = f762; p. 573 = f763; p. 574 = f764; p. 577 = f769 (views f767-f768 are the plate and its blank). The Gallica text layer (texteBrut) was blocked by an anti-bot page, so every quote below is transcribed from the page images. Long s (ſ) is rendered as s.
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "Loi fondamentale de l'Électricité. La force répulsive de deux petits globes électrisés de la même nature d'électricité, est en raison inverse du carré de la distance du centre des deux globes." (p. 572; heading and statement in italic) [translation: "Fundamental law of electricity. The repulsive force between two small spheres electrified with the same kind of electricity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the centers of the two spheres." — my rendering]
  2. "Il résulte donc de ces trois essais, que l'action répulsive que les deux balles électrisées de la même nature d'électricité exercent l'une sur l'autre, suit la raison inverse du carré des distances." (p. 574) [translation: "It follows, then, from these three trials that the repulsive action that the two balls, electrified with the same kind of electricity, exert on each other follows the inverse ratio of the square of the distances." — my rendering]
  3. "Détermination expérimentale de la loi suivant laquelle les élémens des Corps électrisés du même genre d'Électricité, se repoussent mutuellement." (p. 569, subtitle under the title "PREMIER MÉMOIRE SUR L'ÉLECTRICITÉ ET LE MAGNÉTISME. Par M. COULOMB.") [translation: "Experimental determination of the law by which the elements of bodies electrified with the same kind of electricity repel one another." — my rendering]
  4. Title page (view f1): "HISTOIRE DE L'ACADÉMIE ROYALE DES SCIENCES. ANNÉE M. DCCLXXXV. Avec les Mémoires de Mathématique & de Physique, pour la même Année, Tirés des Registres de cette Académie. A PARIS, DE L'IMPRIMERIE ROYALE. M. DCCLXXXVIII."
- **Claim check**: SUPPORTED. The mémoire states the inverse-square law in its own words (quote 1) and derives it from three torsion-balance trials (quote 2). The SGM sentence uses the magnitude $e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2)$ for two unit charges; the example in the text is two electrons, which repel, so this is the repulsive case the first mémoire measures. The form in the equation (SI units, $4\pi\varepsilon_0$, the elementary charge) is modern notation, not Coulomb's. Coulomb gives a proportionality and no constant. That is the usual convention when this paper is cited for "Coulomb's law".
- **Status**: VERIFIED. The primary text was read from the BnF page images. The law is quoted verbatim from p. 572, its experimental conclusion from p. 574, and the page range 569-577 confirmed: p. 569 opens with the title and "Par M. Coulomb"; p. 577 ends the mémoire with a tailpiece; the footer reads "Mém. 1785".
- **Flags**:
  - Metadata. Pages 569-577 and the year 1785 match the .bib. The year is the Académie's year ("Année 1785"). The volume was printed in 1788 (title page, quote 4). The .bib has no volume or printing-year note; `note = {Ann\'ee 1785, published 1788}` was added on 2026-09-22 so the reference can be found. The .bib journal name "Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences" is the conventional short form. The running head is "Mémoires de l'Académie Royale" and the volume title is "Histoire de l'Académie Royale des Sciences ... avec les Mémoires de Mathématique & de Physique".
  - The archive.org item bub_gb_rIYlBNp4oiIC, which a search returns for this series, is the Année 1786 volume (M.DCCLXXXVI) and not this one. Do not use it as the source.
  - Transcription. In quote 1 the acute accent on the first "e" of "d'électricité" is faint in the scan. I read it as present, as in the same word on p. 574. Otherwise quotes 1-3 are checked character by character against full-resolution crops, with long s normalized to s and the original "élémens" spelling kept.
  - Attraction between unlike charges is not in this mémoire. It is in Coulomb's Second mémoire in the same volume (pp. 578 ff.). That does not matter for the SGM sentence, which uses only the magnitude.

### Poisson1813Remarques
- **Authors**: Siméon Denis Poisson ("M. Poisson"). **Title**: Remarques sur une équation qui se présente dans la théorie des attractions des sphéroïdes. **Journal**: Nouveau Bulletin des Sciences, par la Société Philomathique de Paris, Tome III (5e année), No. 75 (Paris, Décembre 1813), pp. 388-392. No DOI.
- **Claim supported**: "Gauss's law for $\alpha$ ... has the differential form $\nabla^2\alpha = 4\pi G\rho/c^2$ (eq:poisson_alpha), Poisson's equation \citep{Poisson1813Remarques} with the mass density as source." (sgm_core_rewrite.tex L1844, sec:alpha_source)
- **Source URL**: https://archive.org/details/nouveaubulletind03soci (Natural History Museum London copy, scanned for BHL). Pages read as images: https://archive.org/download/nouveaubulletind03soci/page/leaf{N}_w1400.jpg, with title page = leaf 5, p. 377 = leaf 395, and pp. 388-392 = leaves 406-410 (the leaf-to-page mapping is taken from the item's scandata.xml). The OCR text layer (nouveaubulletind03soci_djvu.txt) was used only to locate the pages, because it garbles the equations. Every quote below is transcribed from the page images.
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "Si l'on représente par dm, un élément quelconque de la masse du sphéroïde attirant ; par x, y, z, les trois coordonnées rectangulaires de cette molécule ; par a, b, c, celle du point attiré ; par r, la distance de ce point à l'élément dm ; enfin par V l'intégrale ∫dm/r, étendue à la masse entière, ensorte que l'on ait r² = (x − a)² + (y − b)² + (z − c)², ∫dm/r = V, cette quantité V sera une fonction de a, b, c, qui satisfera, en général, à l'équation d²V/da² + d²V/db² + d²V/dc² = 0, (1) dont M. Laplace a fait la base de ses belles recherches sur l'attraction des sphéroïdes de forme quelconque." (pp. 388-389) [translation: "If dm denotes any element of the mass of the attracting spheroid; x, y, z the three rectangular coordinates of this molecule; a, b, c those of the attracted point; r the distance from this point to the element dm; and finally V the integral ∫dm/r taken over the whole mass, so that r² = ..., ∫dm/r = V, then this quantity V will be a function of a, b, c that satisfies, in general, the equation d²V/da² + d²V/db² + d²V/dc² = 0, (1) on which Laplace based his fine researches on the attraction of spheroids of arbitrary shape." — my rendering]
  2. "mais il n'est cependant pas inutile d'observer qu'elle ne serait plus vraie, si le point attiré était un des points de la masse du sphéroïde" (p. 389) [translation: "but it is nevertheless worth observing that it would no longer be true if the attracted point were one of the points of the mass of the spheroid" — my rendering]
  3. "π désignant le rapport de la circonférence au diamètre, et ρ la densité. Au moyen de ces valeurs, on trouve − 4πρ pour celle du second membre de l'équation (2) ; cette équation deviendra donc d²V/da² + d²V/db² + d²V/dc² = − 4πρ. (3)" (p. 390) [translation: "π denoting the ratio of the circumference to the diameter, and ρ the density. With these values one finds −4πρ for the right-hand side of equation (2); this equation therefore becomes d²V/da² + d²V/db² + d²V/dc² = −4πρ. (3)" — my rendering]
  4. "Si le sphéroïde est hétérogène, et même si la densité varie d'une manière continue dans son intérieur, cette équation (3) aura encore lieu, pourvu qu'alors ρ désigne la densité à l'endroit où est placé le point attiré." (p. 390, case 2°) [translation: "If the spheroid is heterogeneous, and even if the density varies continuously in its interior, this equation (3) will still hold, provided that ρ then denotes the density at the location of the attracted point." — my rendering]
  5. "Concluons donc de tout ce qui précède, que les équations (3) et (1) ont lieu pour un sphéroïde de forme et de nature quelconques : la première, quand le point attiré fait partie de la masse de ce corps ; et la seconde, dans le cas contraire." (p. 391) [translation: "Let us therefore conclude from all the foregoing that equations (3) and (1) hold for a spheroid of any shape and constitution: the first when the attracted point is part of the mass of the body, and the second otherwise." — my rendering]
  6. Issue masthead (p. 377, leaf 395): "NOUVEAU BULLETIN DES SCIENCES, PAR LA SOCIÉTÉ PHILOMATIQUE. PARIS. Décembre 1813." with "No. 75." at the top right and the signature line "Tom. III. No. 75. 6e. Année." Table of contents (Mathématiques): "Remarques sur une équation qui se présente dans la théorie des attractions des sphéroïdes ; par M. Poisson. 388".
- **Claim check**: SUPPORTED. Equation (3) on p. 390 is Poisson's equation with the local mass density as source (quotes 3-5). It is the first statement that the Laplacian of the Newtonian potential equals −4πρ inside matter rather than zero. The sign and constant differ from the SGM form only by convention: Poisson's V = ∫dm/r is positive and has no G, so with Φ = −GV, equation (3) becomes ∇²Φ = 4πGρ. The SGM relation ∇²α = 4πGρ/c² follows because the weak-field α deficit is |Φ|/c² (eq:alpha_weak), so α − 1 = Φ/c². The step from Poisson's V to the SGM's α is the paper's own and is not in Poisson.
- **Status**: VERIFIED. The primary text was read from page images of Tome III. The equation is quoted verbatim with its number (3) and page (390). The metadata (volume, pages, issue date) is confirmed from the title page, the No. 75 masthead, the contents list, and "Fin du Tome troisième" at the foot of p. 392.
- **Flags**:
  - Metadata. Volume 3, pages 388-392 and year 1813 match the .bib. The note is in No. 75, dated December 1813; `number = {75}` was added to the .bib on 2026-09-22. The volume title page reads "TOME IIIe. 5e. Année ... M. DCCC. XII.—", with "1813" added by hand, because the volume spans 1812-1813; the signature line of No. 75 says "6e. Année". Neither affects the .bib year of 1813, which is the issue date. The volume title page reads "Société Philomatique de Paris", which the .bib follows (the issue masthead omits "de Paris").
  - The printed notation is Leibniz d for the partial derivatives (d²V/da² ...), with (a, b, c) as the coordinates of the attracted point. The quotes render it in linear form. The fraction bars are in the original.
  - On p. 392 Poisson refers to "l'équation (3)", which the scan prints in a form that resembles "(5)". It is not quoted.
  - The archive.org OCR mislabels No. 75 as "Tom. II". The image reads "Tom. III".

### Lamb1947Fine
- **Authors**: Willis E. Lamb, Jr., Robert C. Retherford. **Title**: Fine Structure of the Hydrogen Atom by a Microwave Method. **Journal**: Physical Review 72(3), 241-243 (1947). **DOI**: 10.1103/PhysRev.72.241.
- **Claim supported**: "The measured spectrum has the pattern of Eq.~\eqref{eq:fine_structure}, with $2S_{1/2}$ and $2P_{1/2}$ together apart from the much smaller Lamb shift \citep{Lamb1947Fine}." (sgm_core_rewrite.tex L1103). The preceding text says that the Dirac fine structure depends on j alone, whereas Klein-Gordon separates 2S from 2P.
- **Source URL**: https://link.aps.org/pdf/10.1103/PhysRev.72.241 (APS published version, listed by Unpaywall as free to read; read from the OpenAlex cached copy of that PDF, 3 pages). Quotes are transcribed from the page images.
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "According to the Dirac theory, this state exactly coincides in energy with the 2²P½ state which is the lower of the two P states." (p. 241; "this state" is 2²S½)
  2. "It has been considered one of the great triumphs of Dirac's theory that it gave the "right" fine structure of the energy levels." (p. 241)
  3. "The calculated separation between the levels 2²P½ and 2²P3/2 is 0.365 cm⁻¹" (p. 241)
  4. "The results indicate clearly that, contrary to theory but in essential agreement with Pasternack's hypothesis,³ the 2²S½ state is higher than the 2²P½ by about 1000 Mc/sec. (0.033 cm⁻¹ or about 9 percent of the spin relativity doublet separation." (p. 242; the parenthesis is unclosed in the original [sic])
  5. "With the present precision, we have not yet detected any discrepancy between the Dirac theory and the doublet separation of the P levels." (p. 243)
- **Claim check**: SUPPORTED. Lamb and Retherford measured 2S½ above 2P½ by about 1000 Mc/s, which is 0.033 cm⁻¹ against a 0.365 cm⁻¹ fine-structure doublet, or about 9 percent (quotes 3-4). Dirac predicts exact degeneracy (quote 1), and the P doublet agrees with Dirac (quote 5). So the measured n=2 levels have Dirac's j-only pattern, with 2S½ and 2P½ together apart from a shift about an order of magnitude smaller than the fine structure, as the SGM sentence says. "Much smaller" is accurate: the factor is about 11.
- **Status**: VERIFIED. The published full text was read, with verbatim quotes and locators.
- **Flags**:
  - Metadata matches the .bib and Crossref: vol. 72, issue 3, pp. 241-243, 1 August 1947.
  - INSPIRE also lists a reprint in Schwinger (ed.), Selected Papers on Quantum Electrodynamics (Dover, 1958), pp. 136-138. This is not needed in the .bib.
  - The OpenAlex cached-copy URL contains an API key and is intentionally not recorded here.

### CarrRees1979Anthropic
- **Authors**: B. J. Carr, M. J. Rees. **Title**: The anthropic principle and the structure of the physical world. **Journal**: Nature 278(5705), 605-612 (12 April 1979). **DOI**: 10.1038/278605a0.
- **Claim supported**: "The ratio $GMm/(\hbar c)$ is the dimensionless gravitational coupling constant, the generalization to two arbitrary masses of the gravitational fine-structure constant that \citet{CarrRees1979Anthropic} define for two protons. For two equal masses it is the square of the mass in units of $m_P$..." (sgm_core_rewrite.tex L1526; reworded 2026-09-22 after the check below, which found the earlier wording credited Carr and Rees with the two-mass form)
- **Source URL**: https://www.nature.com/articles/278605a0 (landing page with the standfirst only; the article is paywalled). The full text was read from a shadow-library copy of the publisher PDF (8 pages, an image scan with no text layer). The copy is kept only in the session scratchpad for verification and is not in the repository. Quotes are transcribed visually from rendered page images.
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "The basic features of galaxies, stars, planets and the everyday world are essentially determined by a few microphysical constants and by the effects of gravitation. Many interrelations between different scales that at first sight seem surprising are straightforward consequences of simple physical arguments. But several aspects of our Universe—some of which seem to be prerequisites for the evolution of any form of life—depend rather delicately on apparent 'coincidences' among the physical constants." (p. 605, standfirst; identical on the Nature landing page)
  2. "In particular, the mass scale and length scale (in units of the proton mass m_P and the Bohr radius a_0) of all structures down to the atom can be expressed in terms of the electromagnetic fine structure constant, α = e²/ħc, the gravitational fine structure constant, α_G = Gm_P²/ħc and the electron-to-proton mass ratio, m_e/m_p." (p. 605, col. 1)
  3. "The Planck scales: the only quantities of dimensions mass and length which can be constructed from G, ħ and c are the Planck scales: M_Pl ~ (G/ħc)^{−1/2} ~ 10⁻⁵ g   R_Pl ~ (G/ħc³)^{1/2} ~ 10⁻³³ cm (7). By introducing the gravitational fine structure constant, α_G ≡ Gm_p²/ħc ≈ 5×10⁻³⁹ (8) these scales can be expressed as M_Pl ~ α_G^{−1/2} m_p   R_Pl ~ α_G^{1/2} r_p (9)" (p. 606)
- **Claim check**: SUPPORTED, with a wording flag. Carr and Rees define the dimensionless gravitational coupling α_G = Gm_p²/ħc (quotes 2-3) and relate it to the Planck mass by M_Pl ~ α_G^{−1/2} m_p (quote 3). With M_Pl = (ħc/G)^{1/2} exactly, α_G = (m_p/M_Pl)², which is the "square of the mass in Planck units" statement in the SGM sentence. Three differences between the paper and the SGM wording:
  - (a) Carr and Rees call α_G the "gravitational fine structure constant", not the "gravitational coupling constant". Both names are in use.
  - (b) They define it only for the proton mass. The two-mass form GMm/(ħc) is the SGM paper's generalization and is not in Carr and Rees.
  - (c) Their subscript P/p means the proton, whereas the SGM paper's $m_P$ is the Planck mass. A reader comparing the two could confuse them.
  - Their Planck relations use "~" (order of magnitude). The exact identity is the SGM paper's, and it is elementary.
- **Status**: VERIFIED. The full text was read (from a scan), with the definition quoted verbatim with its page and equation number (8).
- **Flags**:
  - The attribution is fair for the concept and the name α_G, but not for the general-mass ratio. Suggested rewording: "The ratio $GMm/(\hbar c)$ generalizes the gravitational fine-structure constant $\alpha_G=Gm_p^2/(\hbar c)$ \citep{CarrRees1979Anthropic} to two arbitrary masses; for two equal masses it is the square of the mass in units of $m_P$ ...".
  - Metadata matches the .bib and Crossref: vol. 278, issue 5705, pp. 605-612, April 1979. The article is labeled "review article".
  - No free full text was found through open indexes, paperclip, or web search.

### Fulling1973Nonuniqueness
- **Authors**: Stephen A. Fulling. **Title**: Nonuniqueness of Canonical Field Quantization in Riemannian Space-Time. **Journal**: Physical Review D 7(10), 2850-2862 (15 May 1973). **DOI**: 10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2850.
- **Claim supported**: "...registers excitation and de-excitation in the Boltzmann ratio $e^{-2\pi\Omega_dc/a}$, the $2\pi$ entering through the Fourier transform of the chirp \citep{AlsingMilonni2004Simplified}, that is, at the Unruh temperature $k_BT=\hbar a/(2\pi c)$ \citep{Fulling1973Nonuniqueness,Davies1975Scalar,Unruh1976Notes}." (sgm_core_rewrite.tex L2130)
- **Source URL**: abstract from https://inspirehep.net/api/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2850 (INSPIRE-HEP record with the APS abstract). The full text was read from a shadow-library copy of the APS PDF (13 pages, 770273 bytes, with a text layer). The copy is kept only in the session scratchpad for verification and is not in the repository.
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "We point out and discuss an ambiguity which arises in the quantum theory of fields when the background metric is not explicitly Minkowskian-in other words, when an external gravitational field, real or apparent, is present. ... It is applied to a portion of two-dimensional flat space-time equipped with a non-Cartesian space-time coordinate system with respect to which the metric is nonetheless static. The resulting particle interpretation of the field is shown to be different from the standard one in special-relativistic free-field theory." (abstract; the ellipsis marks omitted sentences)
  2. "U(j, k) = [2πω_k(1 − e^{−2πj})]^{−1/2}[(ω_k + k)/m]^{ij}, V(j, k) = [2πω_k(e^{2πj} − 1)]^{−1/2}[(ω_k + k)/m]^{ij}." (p. 2854, Sec. II.C "Inequivalence of the Particle Structures", Eq. (31))
  3. "The crucial point is that the kernel V(j, k) does not vanish, so that Eq. (30) for a_j includes creation operators. A vector which is annihilated by the b's is not annihilated by the a's, and vice versa. The vacuum of the Rindler-space theory is not the ordinary vacuum of the free field, one-particle states in one theory are not one-particle states in the other theory, and so on. The notion of a particle is completely different in the two theories. The particles or quanta of the Rindler-Fock representation cannot be identified with the physical particles described by the usual quantum theory of the free field." (p. 2854; the last sentence is italic in the original)
  4. "Rindler coordinates are just as appropriate for the description of the region of flat space which they cover as Schwarzschild coordinates are for the study of the space around a massive body outside the radius r = 2M. If the theory fails in this test case, it probably must also be rejected for the Schwarzschild metric." (p. 2855)
  5. Secondary attribution (Crispino, Higuchi, Matsas, "The Unruh effect and its applications", Rev. Mod. Phys. 80, 787-838 (2008), DOI 10.1103/RevModPhys.80.787, confirmed on Crossref; arXiv:0710.5373 source, rmpfinalsub.tex):
     - "It has been thirty years since the discovery of the {\em Unruh effect} \cite{Unruh76} which can be also found under the name of {\em Davies-Unruh, Fulling-Davies-Unruh, {\rm and} Unruh-Davies-DeWitt-Fulling effect}. This is a conceptually subtle quantum field theory result, which has played a crucial role in our understanding that the particle content of a field theory is observer dependent in a sense to be made precise later \cite{Fulling73} [see also \textcite{Unruh77}]." (Sec. I, L79-85)
     - "As was observed by \textcite{Fulling73}, this vacuum state is not the same as the state obtained by restricting the usual Minkowski vacuum to this region." (L649-651)
     - "by explicit evaluation of the Bogolubov coefficients, which were originally computed by \textcite{Fulling73}." (L1480-1481)
- **Claim check**: SUPPORTED as part of the standard joint attribution. Fulling contributes the inequivalent Rindler quantization of flat space-time (quotes 1, 3) and the Bogoliubov coefficients (quote 2). Their ratio |V/U|² = e^{−2πj} is the Boltzmann factor behind the Unruh temperature. Fulling does not state a temperature or a thermal interpretation: the full text layer has 0 matches for "thermal", "temperature", "Boltzmann" and "heat bath", against 28 for "Rindler". Co-citing Fulling, Davies and Unruh for the Unruh temperature is the standard attribution: the effect is known as the "Fulling-Davies-Unruh effect", and Crispino et al. credit Fulling with the observer dependence of particle content and the first computation of the Bogoliubov coefficients (quote 5). Strictly, the temperature itself is Davies's (for a mirror) and Unruh's (for a detector in vacuum), not Fulling's.
- **Status**: VERIFIED. The full text was read, with verbatim quotes and page and equation locators, and the secondary attribution is quoted from Crispino et al. 2008.
- **Flags**:
  - Metadata matches the .bib and Crossref: vol. 7, issue 10, pp. 2850-2862, 1973. Crossref capitalizes the title as "Nonuniqueness of Canonical Field Quantization in Riemannian Space-Time". The .bib uses sentence case with "{R}iemannian" braced, which is correct.
  - If the paper wants the attribution to be exact, it could say "the Unruh temperature ... \citep{Davies1975Scalar,Unruh1976Notes}, with the underlying inequivalence of Rindler and Minkowski quantization due to \citet{Fulling1973Nonuniqueness}". The current joint citation is conventional and not wrong.
  - No free copy was found through open indexes, paperclip, or web search.

### Davies1975Scalar
- **Authors**: P. C. W. Davies. **Title (as printed)**: Scalar particle production in Schwarzschild and Rindler metrics. **Journal**: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General 8(4), 609-616 (1975). **DOI**: 10.1088/0305-4470/8/4/022.
- **Claim supported**: the same sentence as Fulling1973Nonuniqueness (sgm_core_rewrite.tex L2130): "...at the Unruh temperature $k_BT=\hbar a/(2\pi c)$ \citep{Fulling1973Nonuniqueness,Davies1975Scalar,Unruh1976Notes}."
- **Source URL**: https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0305-4470/8/4/022/pdf (IOP publisher PDF, free to read as bronze open access; read from the OpenAlex cached copy, 9 pages including an IOP cover page). Quotes are transcribed from the page images.
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "The procedure used recently by Hawking to demonstrate the creation of massless particles by black holes is applied to the Rindler coordinate system in flat space-time. The result is that an observer who undergoes a uniform acceleration κ apparently sees a fixed surface radiate with a temperature of κ/2π. Some implications of this result are discussed." (abstract, p. 609)
  2. "Even in flat space-time it is possible to construct (Rindler 1966, Fulling 1972, 1973) a self-consistent quantization scheme based on Rindler (rather than Minkowski) coordinates which differs from the conventional quantization." (p. 609)
  3. "The upshot of this is that the fixed reflecting wall appears to an accelerating observer to radiate at a constant temperature of (ħ/2πkc)×(acceleration) K in cgs units. In geometric units the acceleration may be equated to the surface gravity κ of an object of mass M. In that case the radiation has a temperature of κ/2π which is exactly the temperature of a black hole with surface gravity κ found by Hawking." (pp. 610-611)
  4. "To such an observer the wall surface would appear to have a temperature of (acceleration/2π). From the point of view of the observer O, a wall which recedes with acceleration κ in flat space-time acquires a temperature of κ/2π, which is the same temperature as that acquired by the surface of a collapsing star receding with a (proper) acceleration κ." (p. 614)
  5. Secondary attribution (Crispino, Higuchi, Matsas, Rev. Mod. Phys. 80, 787 (2008), arXiv:0710.5373 source, rmpfinalsub.tex L103-107): "\textcite{Unruh76} also provides an explanation for the conclusion obtained by \textcite{Davies75} that an observer undergoing uniform acceleration $a = {\rm const}$ in Minkowski spacetime would see a fixed inertial mirror to emit thermal radiation with temperature $a \hbar/(2 \pi k c )$, and the reason why this is not in contradiction with energy conservation."
- **Claim check**: SUPPORTED. Davies obtains the temperature ħa/(2πkc) for a uniformly accelerated observer (quote 3; κ/2π in geometric units, quotes 1 and 4). This is the SGM paper's $k_BT=\hbar a/(2\pi c)$. Crispino et al. confirm the attribution and the value (quote 5). Davies's setup is a fixed reflecting mirror treated by Hawking's collapse method, not a detector in the bare vacuum. The detector interpretation that the SGM sentence describes ("registers excitation and de-excitation") is Unruh's (1976), who also explains Davies's result (quote 5). Co-citing Davies for the temperature is the standard attribution (Crispino et al. name the effect "Davies-Unruh" and "Fulling-Davies-Unruh"; see the Fulling record).
- **Status**: VERIFIED. The full text was read, with verbatim quotes and page locators, and the secondary attribution is quoted.
- **Flags**:
  - **Title discrepancy.** The printed title is "Scalar *particle* production in Schwarzschild and Rindler metrics". The .bib, following Crossref, has "Scalar production in {S}chwarzschild and {R}indler metrics", which omits "particle". The bibliography in Crispino et al. uses the printed title. The .bib title was corrected to "Scalar particle production in {S}chwarzschild and {R}indler metrics" on 2026-09-22, after the orchestrator checked the printed title on the page image of p. 609.
  - Volume 8, issue 4, pp. 609-616, 1975 and the DOI match the .bib. The paper was received 23 August 1974, final form 14 October 1974, from King's College London.
  - **Transcription.** In quote 3 the bar on ħ is faint: it is visible at 800 dpi but the 300 dpi scan looks like plain h, and the PDF text layer reads "h". Read as h, the value would be 2π too large. The reading ħ is confirmed by the geometric-units κ/2π in the same passage and in the abstract, and by Crispino et al.'s restatement aħ/(2πkc).
  - The OpenAlex cached-copy URL contains an API key and is intentionally not recorded here.

Records for groups A and B of Codex F21 follow. Quotes marked "checked against the image" or "page image" were read from scans; the orchestrator re-read the Einstein 1907 S. 457 and Moller p. 255 page images, the Hamilton essay TeX and the Fermat tome II text before applying the changes marked APPLIED.

### Doppler1842Farbige (new entry)
- **Authors**: Christian Doppler. **Title**: Ueber das farbige Licht der Doppelsterne und einiger anderer Gestirne des Himmels. Versuch einer das Bradley'sche Aberrations-Theorem als integrirenden Theil in sich schliessenden allgemeineren Theorie. **Journal**: Abhandlungen der k. böhm. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften, V. Folge, Bd. 2, 465-482 (1842). **DOI**: none.
- **Claim supported**: "Its physical content is a Doppler shift \citep{Doppler1842Farbige}" (sgm_core_rewrite L494): the read rate of the phase is shifted by the motion of the receiver relative to the source.
- **Source URL**: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Doppelsterne_(Doppler)_1842 (scan of the 1842 separate offprint, "Doppler (1842) 001.jpg" etc., own pagination; title page and pp. 5-6 read visually) + https://de.wikisource.org/wiki/Über_das_farbige_Licht_der_Doppelsterne_und_einiger_anderer_Gestirne_des_Himmels (transcription of the Studnička 1903 Prague reprint; bracketed numbers are reprint pages)
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "In der That scheint nichts begreiflicher, als dass der Weg und die Zwischenzeit zweier aufeinanderfolgender Wellenschläge für einen Beobachter sich verkürzen muss, wenn der Beobachter der ankommenden Welle entgegeneilt, und verlängern, wenn er ihr enteilt, und dass auch gleichzeitig im ersteren Falle die Intensität des Wellenschlags grösser werden, im zweiten dagegen nothwendig sich vermindern muss. Bei einer Bewegung der Wellenquelle selbst findet natürlich eine ähnliche Veränderung in demselben Sinne statt." (§ 2, offprint S. 5; reprint S. 8; checked against the offprint scan) [translation: "Indeed nothing seems more comprehensible than that the path and the interval between two successive wave crests must shorten for an observer when the observer hurries toward the arriving wave, and lengthen when he hurries away from it, and that at the same time the intensity of the wave crest must become greater in the first case and necessarily diminish in the second. When the wave source itself moves, a similar change naturally occurs in the same sense." — my rendering]
  2. "Man hat daher für den Fall der Annäherung sowohl wie der Entfernung des Beobachters von oder an die Quelle, wegen ax'' ± αx = an''; 1, x'' = an/(a ± α)" (§ 3, Fall 1, formula (1), offprint S. 6; reprint S. 9; checked against the offprint scan) [translation: "One therefore has, for the case of approach as well as recession of the observer from or toward the source, because ax'' ± αx = an''; 1, x'' = an/(a ± α)" — my rendering; per the Wikisource note, x'' and n'' denote times in seconds, a the wave speed, α the observer's speed]
  3. "Abhandlungen der k. böhm. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften (V. Folge, Bd. 2, S. 465-482) (ursprünglicher Aufsatz)" (Wikisource header of the transcription; secondary confirmation of the journal pagination)
- **Claim check**: L494 ("Its physical content is a Doppler shift") SUPPORTED. Doppler states that a receiver moving toward the arriving waves receives shortened intervals (a blueshift) and that a moving source gives a change in the same sense (quote 1), and gives the moving-observer formula (quote 2). His formula is classical, for waves in a medium, not relativistic; that is adequate for an attribution of the Doppler principle itself.
- **Status**: VERIFIED (metadata from the 1842 offprint title page and the Wikisource header) with primary-source quotes (offprint scan pp. 5-6, Wikisource transcription of the 1903 reprint).
- **Flags**: (a) The original title spelling is "Ueber", not "Über" as in the .bib; the modernized spelling is a common convention, but the 1842 title page reads "Ueber". (b) The .bib omits "V. Folge" (5th series); "volume 2" alone is ambiguous across the series of the Abhandlungen. Suggest `volume = {2}, series = {5}` or a note "V. Folge, Bd. 2". (c) The .bib journal name "Abhandlungen der Königlich Böhmischen Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften" expands the imprint's "k. böhm."; acceptable. (d) The journal pages 465-482 are confirmed only from the Wikisource header (quote 3), not from a scan of the journal volume itself; I read the separately paginated offprint. The offprint-to-journal page offset (presumably +464) is inferred, not confirmed. (e) Fall 2 in the offprint scan misprints "(Q ∓ α)/a" in formula (2); Wikisource corrects it to (a ∓ α)/a. Not quoted here.

### Einstein1907Relativitatsprinzip (new entry)
- **Authors**: A. Einstein. **Title**: Über das Relativitätsprinzip und die aus demselben gezogenen Folgerungen. **Journal**: Jahrbuch der Radioaktivität und Elektronik 4, 411-462 (1907); Berichtigungen in Jahrbuch 5, 98-99 (1908). **DOI**: none.
- **Claim supported**: (i) "The local equivalence of gravity and acceleration is Einstein's founding hypothesis" (L74); (ii) the rate of proper time relative to coordinate time varies with position (L150, joint cite with Einstein1911Influence, Pound1960Apparent, Bothwell2022Resolving); (iii) "\citet{Einstein1907Relativitatsprinzip} obtained it to first order in a0 ξ/c²" (L494, after the fix below; the exactness claim is now cited to Moller1952Theory, Rindler1966Kruskal, MTW1973Gravitation only); (iv) "a gravitational field and a uniformly accelerating frame are locally indistinguishable, which is the equivalence principle" (L565).
- **Source URL**: https://archive.org/details/jahrbuch-der-radioaktivitat-und-elektronik-4.1907 (djvu OCR plus page images read visually at leaves n418 = S. 411, n461 = S. 454, n464 = S. 457, n465 = S. 458) + https://archive.org/details/jahrbuch-der-radioaktivitat-und-elektronik-5.1908 (Berichtigungen; leaf n110 = S. 99 read visually)
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "Wir betrachten zwei Bewegungssysteme Σ₁ und Σ₂. Σ₁ sei in Richtung seiner X-Achse beschleunigt, und es sei γ die (zeitlich konstante) Größe dieser Beschleunigung. Σ₂ sei ruhend; es befinde sich aber in einem homogenen Gravitationsfelde, das allen Gegenständen die Beschleunigung — γ in Richtung der X-Achse erteilt." (§ 17, S. 454; checked against the image) [translation: "We consider two systems of motion Σ₁ and Σ₂. Let Σ₁ be accelerated in the direction of its X-axis, and let γ be the (temporally constant) magnitude of this acceleration. Let Σ₂ be at rest, but situated in a homogeneous gravitational field that gives all objects the acceleration −γ in the direction of the X-axis." — my rendering]
  2. "Wir haben daher bei dem gegenwärtigen Stande unserer Erfahrung keinen Anlaß zu der Annahme, daß sich die Systeme Σ₁ und Σ₂ in irgendeiner Beziehung voneinander unterscheiden, und wollen daher im folgenden die völlige physikalische Gleichwertigkeit von Gravitationsfeld und entsprechender Beschleunigung des Bezugssystems annehmen." (§ 17, S. 454) [translation: "In the present state of our experience we therefore have no reason to assume that the systems Σ₁ and Σ₂ differ from each other in any respect, and in what follows we shall therefore assume the complete physical equivalence of a gravitational field and the corresponding acceleration of the reference system." — my rendering]
  3. "Diese Annahme erweitert das Prinzip der Relativität auf den Fall der gleichförmig beschleunigten Translationsbewegung des Bezugssystems." (§ 17, S. 454) [translation: "This assumption extends the principle of relativity to the case of uniformly accelerated translational motion of the reference system." — my rendering]
  4. "Wir beschränken uns nun zunächst auf die Betrachtung so kurzer Zeiten¹), daß alle Glieder, welche die zweite oder eine höhere Potenz von τ oder v enthalten, weggelassen werden dürfen" (§ 18, S. 457; checked against the image) [translation: "We now restrict ourselves at first to the consideration of times so short that all terms containing the second or a higher power of τ or v may be omitted" — my rendering]; footnote 1 on S. 457: "Hierdurch wird gemäß (1) auch eine gewisse Beschränkung in bezug auf die Werte von ξ = x' angenommen." [translation: "By this, according to (1), a certain restriction on the values of ξ = x' is also assumed." — my rendering]
  5. "σ = τ(1 + γξ/c²). (30) Diese Gleichung gilt zunächst, wenn τ und ξ unterhalb gewisser Grenzen liegen. Sie gilt offenbar für beliebig große τ, falls die Beschleunigung γ mit Bezug auf Σ konstant ist, weil die Beziehung zwischen σ und τ dann linear sein muß. Für beliebig große ξ gilt Gleichung (30) nicht. Daraus, daß die Wahl des Koordinatenanfangspunktes auf die Relation nicht von Einfluß sein darf, schließt man nämlich, daß die Gleichung (30) genau genommen durch die Gleichung σ = τ e^{γξ/c²} ersetzt werden müßte. Wir wollen jedoch an der Formel (30) festhalten." (§ 18, S. 457; checked against the image) [translation: "σ = τ(1 + γξ/c²). (30) This equation holds at first when τ and ξ lie below certain limits. It evidently holds for arbitrarily large τ if the acceleration γ is constant with respect to Σ, because the relation between σ and τ must then be linear. For arbitrarily large ξ, Eq. (30) does not hold. From the fact that the choice of the coordinate origin must not affect the relation, one concludes that, strictly speaking, Eq. (30) would have to be replaced by the equation σ = τ e^{γξ/c²}. We shall, however, keep to formula (30)." — my rendering]
  6. "Gleichung (30) ist nach § 17 auch auf ein Koordinatensytem anzuwenden, in dem ein homogenes Schwerfeld wirkt. In diesem Falle haben wir Φ = γξ zu setzen, wobei Φ das Potential der Schwerkraft bedeutet, so daß wir erhalten σ = τ(1 + Φ/c²) (30a)" (§ 18, S. 457; "Koordinatensytem" is the original's typo) [translation: "By § 17, Eq. (30) also applies to a coordinate system in which a homogeneous gravitational field acts. In this case we must put Φ = γξ, where Φ is the gravitational potential, so that we obtain σ = τ(1 + Φ/c²) (30a)" — my rendering]
  7. "Befindet sich in einem Punkte P vom Gravitationspotential Φ eine Uhr, welche die Ortszeit angibt, so sind gemäß (30a) ihre Angaben (1 + Φ/c²) mal größer als die Zeit τ, d. h. sie läuft (1 + Φ/c²) mal schneller als eine gleich beschaffene, im Koordinatenanfangspunkt befindliche Uhr." (§ 19, S. 458; checked against the image) [translation: "If at a point P of gravitational potential Φ there is a clock showing the local time, then by (30a) its readings are (1 + Φ/c²) times greater than the time τ, i.e., it runs (1 + Φ/c²) times faster than an identically constructed clock at the coordinate origin." — my rendering]
  8. "In diesem Sinne können wir sagen, daß der in der Uhr sich abspielende Vorgang — und allgemeiner jeder physikalische Prozeß — desto schneller abläuft, je größer das Gravitationspotential des Ortes ist, an dem er sich abspielt." (§ 19, S. 458-459) [translation: "In this sense we can say that the process taking place in the clock, and more generally every physical process, runs faster the greater the gravitational potential of the place where it takes place." — my rendering]
  9. "Die auf S. 457 gebrauchte Beziehung v = γt gilt also nur in erster Annäherung; dies genügt aber, weil in der Betrachtung nur bezüglich t bezw. τ lineare Glieder zu berücksichtigen sind." (Berichtigungen, Jahrbuch 5, S. 99, 1908; checked against the image) [translation: "The relation v = γt used on p. 457 therefore holds only to a first approximation; this suffices, however, because in the argument only terms linear in t or τ need be taken into account." — my rendering]
- **Claim check**:
  - L74 ("Einstein's founding hypothesis") SUPPORTED: quotes 1-3 state the hypothesis of complete physical equivalence of a homogeneous gravitational field and a uniformly accelerated frame, as an extension of the relativity principle.
  - L565 ("locally indistinguishable ... equivalence principle") SUPPORTED: quotes 1-3. Einstein states it for a homogeneous field and uniform acceleration; "locally" is the later reading of that restriction and is standard.
  - L150 (proper-time rate varies with position) SUPPORTED as a joint cite: quotes 6-8 give a clock rate that depends on the gravitational potential at the clock's position. The phrase "according to the presence and distribution of mass" is general relativity and rests on the co-cites; Einstein 1907 extends (30a) to non-homogeneous fields only as an assumption (footnote on S. 459: "Indem man voraussetzt, daß Gleichung (30a) auch für ein nichthomogenes Gravitationsfeld gelte", read from the OCR only).
  - L494 ("The factor is exact for a Born-rigid state at every separation with a0 ξ > −c²") NOT SUPPORTED by Einstein 1907. Eq. (30) is derived only to first order (quote 4, and the 1908 correction, quote 9); Einstein says it holds only for ξ below certain limits and fails for arbitrarily large ξ, proposes an exponential as the exact form, and then keeps the linear formula (quote 5). Einstein 1907 therefore does not assert that the linear factor 1 + a0 ξ/c² is exact at every separation; it asserts the opposite for large ξ. The orchestrator checked quote 5 against the S. 457 page image. APPLIED 2026-09-22: Einstein1907 was removed from the exactness cite, and L494 now reads "\citet{Einstein1907Relativitatsprinzip} obtained it to first order in $a_0\,\xi/c^2$", which quotes 4, 5 and 9 support.
- **Status**: VERIFIED (metadata: title page S. 411, end of paper S. 462 "Eingegangen 4. Dezember 1907") with primary-source quotes from the Jahrbuch scans. L74, L150, L565 supported; L494 not supported.
- **Flags**: (a) Recommend removing Einstein1907Relativitatsprinzip from the L494 cite list (Møller §97 eq. (137) supports the exact claim directly; see Moller1952Theory), or rewording to "to first order, as in Einstein (1907)". (b) Einstein's exponential σ = τ e^{γξ/c²} and the linear Rindler lapse are not in conflict; they use different spatial coordinates. With ds² = −(1 + gx/c²)² c² dt² + dx² (x = proper distance) and 1 + gx/c² = e^{gX/c²}, one gets dx = e^{gX/c²} dX and ds² = e^{2gX/c²}(−c² dt² + dX²), so the lapse is exactly e^{gX/c²} in the conformal coordinate X. This is my own algebra (inferred reading of Einstein's ξ; Einstein does not state which coordinate he means). In proper distance, the linear factor is exact, which is the SGM statement. (c) The .bib metadata matches the scan (title with "Über", vol. 4, pp. 411-462, 1907). Suggest adding a note on the Berichtigungen, Jahrb. Radioakt. Elektron. 5, 98-99 (1908), which correct §§ 17-18.

### Born1909Theorie (new entry)
- **Authors**: Max Born. **Title**: Die Theorie des starren Elektrons in der Kinematik des Relativitätsprinzips. **Journal**: Annalen der Physik 335 (ser. 4 vol. 30), no. 11, 1-56 (1909). **DOI**: 10.1002/andp.19093351102.
- **Claim supported**: "Exact rigidity is Born rigidity \citep{Born1909Theorie,Moller1952Theory,Rindler1966Kruskal}, in which the proper acceleration varies along the state as a(ξ) = a0/(1 + a0 ξ/c²): trailing points accelerate harder, and the profile diverges at ξ = −c²/a0." (L482)
- **Source URL**: https://archive.org/details/sim_annalen-der-physik_1909_30_11 (full issue scan; leaves 8, 21, 22, 31, 32, 33, 63 = pp. 1, 14, 15, 24, 25, 26, 56 read visually) + https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/andp.19093351102 (metadata)
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "In den kleinsten Teilen starr werden wir einen Faden nennen, dessen Ruhgestalt von der Eigenzeit τ unabhängig ist, d. h. für den die sechs Gleichungen (38) ∂p_αβ/∂τ = 0 bestehen." (§ 2, p. 15; first clause italic in the original) [translation: "We shall call a thread rigid in its smallest parts if its rest shape is independent of the proper time τ, i.e., if the six equations (38) ∂p_αβ/∂τ = 0 hold for it." — my rendering]
  2. "Die geradlinige Bewegung eines starren Körpers ist also so beschaffen, daß, sobald man einen Punkt auf Ruhe transformiert, durch dieselbe Transformation seine sämtlichen Punkte auf Ruhe transformiert werden." (§ 4, p. 24) [translation: "The rectilinear motion of a rigid body is thus such that, as soon as one point is transformed to rest, the same transformation transforms all its points to rest." — my rendering]
  3. "Die Geraden gleicher Geschwindigkeit p = konst. haben, außer bei gleichförmiger Bewegung, immer eine Enveloppe; an dieser hört die Regularität der Bewegung auf. Bei gegebenen Dimensionen des Körpers kann also die Krümmung der Weltlinien eine gewisse Grenze nicht überschreiten, und umgekehrt. Daraus folgt, daß ein starrer Körper notwendig nach allen Seiten endlich ausgedehnt ist und um so kleiner sein muß, je größere Beschleunigungen er erfahren soll." (§ 4, p. 24; last sentence italic in the original) [translation: "The straight lines of equal velocity p = const. always have an envelope, except in uniform motion; at this envelope the regularity of the motion ceases. For given dimensions of the body, the curvature of the world lines therefore cannot exceed a certain limit, and conversely. It follows that a rigid body is necessarily of finite extent in all directions and must be the smaller, the greater the accelerations it is to undergo." — my rendering]
  4. "(76) x² − c²t² = ξ². Hieraus erkennt man, daß die zugehörigen Weltlinien in der xt-Ebene und den dazu parallelen Ebenen y = η, z = ζ Hyperbeln sind, welche die der Lichtgeschwindigkeit entsprechenden Geraden durch den Nullpunkt zu Asymptoten haben und die x-Achse im Abstande ξ vom Nullpunkte schneiden." (§ 5, p. 25) [translation: "(76) x² − c²t² = ξ². From this one sees that the corresponding world lines in the xt-plane and the planes parallel to it, y = η, z = ζ, are hyperbolas that have as asymptotes the straight lines through the origin corresponding to the speed of light and that cut the x-axis at the distance ξ from the origin." — my rendering]
  5. "Diese, der gleichförmig beschleunigten der alten Kinematik einigermaßen analoge Bewegung, wollen wir kurz die Hyperbelbewegung nennen." (§ 5, p. 25) [translation: "This motion, somewhat analogous to the uniformly accelerated motion of the old kinematics, we shall call hyperbolic motion for short." — my rendering]
  6. "(82) b = √(b_x² − c²b_t²) = c²/ξ der Betrag der Beschleunigung ist." (§ 5, p. 26) [translation: "(82) b = √(b_x² − c²b_t²) = c²/ξ is the magnitude of the acceleration." — my rendering]
  7. "Die Beschleunigung ist also für jede Weltlinie der Hyperbelbewegung dem Betrage nach konstant" (§ 5, p. 26) [translation: "The acceleration is thus constant in magnitude for each world line of the hyperbolic motion" — my rendering]
- **Claim check**: L482 SUPPORTED. Born defines rigidity as a rest shape independent of proper time (quote 1), shows that fixing one point of a rigidly moving body fixes all others (quote 2), gives the rigid uniformly accelerated body as a family of hyperbolas x² − c²t² = ξ² (quotes 4-5) with acceleration c²/ξ on each (quotes 6-7), and derives that the envelope of the motion bounds the size of a rigid body inversely with its acceleration (quote 3), which is the divergence the paper mentions. Born does not write a(ξ) = a0/(1 + a0 ξ/c²) explicitly; it follows by putting Born's ξ = c²/a0 + ξ' in b = c²/ξ, giving b = a0/(1 + a0 ξ'/c²), divergent at ξ' = −c²/a0 (my own one-line algebra). Møller §97 eq. (142) states that formula explicitly (see Moller1952Theory), so the joint cite covers it.
- **Status**: VERIFIED (metadata checked against the scan and Crossref) with primary-source quotes read from the Annalen scan.
- **Flags**: (a) The .bib lacked the DOI 10.1002/andp.19093351102. APPLIED 2026-09-22: the DOI was added after the orchestrator checked it against Crossref (vol. 335, no. 11, pp. 1-56). (b) The scan header reads "1909. № 11. ANNALEN DER PHYSIK. VIERTE FOLGE. BAND 30."; the .bib uses the continuous volume 335 (matches Crossref); a note "ser. 4, vol. 30" would help readers of the original. (c) Pages 1-56 confirmed: title on p. 1 ("1. Die Theorie des starren Elektrons in der Kinematik des Relativitätsprinzips; von Max Born." with the dedication "Dem Andenken Hermann Minkowskis gewidmet."), p. 56 ends "(Eingegangen 13. Juni 1909.)"; the issue cover reads "Ausgegeben am 31. August 1909". (d) Born's paper is on the rigid electron; the hyperbolic-motion result is §§ 4-5, a subsection of it. Adding a locator (§§ 4-5, pp. 24-26) to the citation would help.

### Moller1952Theory (new entry)
- **Authors**: C. Møller. **Title**: The Theory of Relativity. **Publisher**: Clarendon Press, Oxford (first edition 1952). **DOI**: none.
- **Claim supported**: (i) Born rigidity with a(ξ) = a0/(1 + a0 ξ/c²), divergent at ξ = −c²/a0 (L482, joint cite with Born1909Theorie, Rindler1966Kruskal); (ii) "The factor is exact for a Born-rigid state at every separation with a·δx = a0 ξ > −c²" (L494, joint cite with Rindler1966Kruskal, MTW1973Gravitation), where the factor is the time-dilation factor α = 1 + a·δx/c² = √(−g00) of the Rindler metric.
- **Source URL**: https://archive.org/details/theoryofrelativi029229mbp (Universal Library scan of the 1955 reprint "from corrected sheets of the first edition" (1952); PDF pages 9-10 (title and imprint), 271 (book p. 253), 273 (p. 255), 274 (p. 256) read visually)
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "A system of reference is called rigid if the distance between two reference points, as measured by standard measuring-rods at rest in the system, is constant in time." (§ 96, p. 253; "rigid" italic in the original)
  2. "ds² = dx²+dy²+dz²−c² dt²(1+gx/c²)². (137)" (§ 97, p. 255)
  3. "In this case the gravitational field is parallel to the x-axis. The conditions (52) are satisfied everywhere except on the plane x = −c²/g, where g₄₄ becomes equal to zero." (§ 97, p. 255)
  4. "In particular, if the motion of the origin O is a hyperbolic motion with the constant rest acceleration g, we have, according to (IV. 159), θ(t) = gt/c, i.e. g(t) = c dθ/dt = g = constant (138). In this case the gravitational field is static, the gravitational potential being χ = −(c²/2)(g₄₄+1) = gx(1 + gx/2c²). (139)" (§ 97, p. 255)
  5. "Thus we see that, relative to I, each reference point with constant values for x, y, z performs a hyperbolic motion in the direction of the X-axis starting at the point X = x, Y = y, Z = z at T = 0, with zero velocity The acceleration in this hyperbolic motion is γ = g/(1+gx/c²) (142) (see § 29)" (§ 97, p. 256; the missing period after "velocity" is as printed)
  6. "For small values of t and x, where we can neglect terms in gx/c² and gt/c of higher than first order, the system of reference R considered here is identical with the system considered at the end of § 95." (§ 97, p. 256)
  7. "THE THEORY OF RELATIVITY BY C. MØLLER PROFESSOR OF MATHEMATICAL PHYSICS IN THE UNIVERSITY OF COPENHAGEN OXFORD AT THE CLARENDON PRESS" (title page) and "FIRST EDITION 1952 REPRINTED LITHOGRAPHICALLY IN GREAT BRITAIN AT THE UNIVERSITY PRESS, OXFORD FROM CORRECTED SHEETS OF THE FIRST EDITION 1955" (imprint page)
- **Claim check**:
  - L482 SUPPORTED: Møller defines rigid reference systems (quote 1) and, for the rigid frame whose origin has constant rest acceleration g, gives the acceleration of each reference point as γ = g/(1 + gx/c²) (quote 5). That is exactly a(ξ) = a0/(1 + a0 ξ/c²) with g = a0, x = ξ; points with x < 0 (trailing) have γ > g, and γ diverges at x = −c²/g, where g₄₄ = 0 (quote 3).
  - L494 SUPPORTED (quotes 2 and 3 checked by the orchestrator against the p. 255 page image): the metric (137) of the rigid frame has √(−g₄₄) = 1 + gx/c² with no approximation (quote 2), and it is regular everywhere except on the plane x = −c²/g (quote 3), i.e., for all gx > −c². Quote 6 confirms that Møller treats (137) as exact and the first-order system of § 95 as its approximation. The factor 1 + a0 ξ/c² is therefore exact for a0 ξ > −c², as stated.
- **Status**: VERIFIED (metadata from the title and imprint pages) with primary-source quotes read from page images of §§ 96-97.
- **Flags**: (a) The scan is the 1955 lithographic reprint "from corrected sheets of the first edition"; page numbers presumably match the 1952 printing (inferred, not confirmed from a 1952 copy). (b) The .bib gives author "Møller, Christian"; the title page reads "C. Møller". Correct, no change needed. (c) The second edition (Oxford 1972) is substantially rewritten; the .bib year 1952 correctly identifies the first edition, and a locator (§ 97, pp. 255-256, eqs. (137), (142)) would help, since section numbers differ between editions. (d) Møller writes the time coordinate as x₄ = ict in parts of the book (e.g. "(X,Y,Z,icT)", p. 253); g₄₄ in quote 3 is in that convention. (e) The scanned archive.org item begins with an unrelated book (W. Brooke Graves, American State Government, PDF pp. 6-8); Møller begins at PDF p. 9.

### Sommerfeld1916Spectral (new entry)
- **Authors**: A. Sommerfeld. **Title**: Zur Quantentheorie der Spektrallinien. **Journal**: Annalen der Physik 356 (ser. 4 vol. 51), no. 17, 1-94 (1916). **DOI**: 10.1002/andp.19163561702.
- **Claim supported**: "α_fs = e²/(4πε0ħc) ≈ 1/137.036 is the fine-structure constant \citep{Sommerfeld1916Spectral}" (L1098) and eq:alpha_crossing, "e²/(4πε0 ħc) = 1/137.036, the fine-structure constant \citep{Sommerfeld1916Spectral}: two unit charges exchange one radian of phase every 137 crossing times" (L2024-2027).
- **Source URL**: https://archive.org/details/sim_annalen-der-physik_1916_51_17 (full issue scan; leaves 8, 58, 59, 60, 98, 99, 101 = pp. 1, 51, 52, 53, 91, 92, 94 read visually) + https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/andp.19163561702 (metadata)
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "Für das Verhältnis p0 : p1 das wir α nennen wollen, ergibt sich (12a) α = p0/p1 = 2πe²/(hc) = rund 7·10⁻³." (II. Teil, § 3, p. 51; checked against the image) [translation: "For the ratio p0 : p1, which we shall call α, we obtain (12a) α = p0/p1 = 2πe²/(hc) = roughly 7·10⁻³." — my rendering]
  2. "Die Größe der Verhältniszahl α, die in allen folgenden Formeln eine wichtige Rolle spielen wird, hat auch ein gewisses literarisches Interesse. Einstein¹) bemerkte gelegentlich, daß die Größe e²/c dieselbe Dimension und Größenordnung wie h habe" (p. 51) [translation: "The magnitude of the ratio α, which will play an important role in all the following formulas, is also of some literary interest. Einstein once remarked that the quantity e²/c has the same dimension and order of magnitude as h" — my rendering]
  3. "Wir sehen jetzt, daß dieser Zahlenfaktor nämlich unser obiges α, die Fundamentalgröße für die Beschreibung der Feinstruktur der Spektrallinien wird." (p. 52) [translation: "We now see that this numerical factor, namely our α above, becomes the fundamental quantity for the description of the fine structure of the spectral lines." — my rendering]
  4. "Wir fügen den Bohrschen Gleichungen (46) und (47) die charakteristische Konstante unserer Feinstrukturen (49) α = 2πe²/(ch) hinzu" (§ 12, p. 91) [translation: "To Bohr's equations (46) and (47) we add the characteristic constant of our fine structures (49) α = 2πe²/(ch)" — my rendering]

The value 1/137.036 is the modern (CODATA) value, not Sommerfeld's: his 1916 values are "rund 7·10⁻³" and (7.25 ± 0.10)·10⁻³, i.e., about 1/138 (my arithmetic: 1/0.00725 = 137.9). The reading "two unit charges exchange one radian of phase every 137 crossing times" (L2029) is the paper's own interpretation and is not in Sommerfeld; the cite supports only the naming of the constant.
- **Status**: VERIFIED (metadata checked against the scan and Crossref: vol. 356, issue 17, pp. 1-94) with primary-source quotes read from page images.
- **Flags**: (a) The .bib metadata matches (vol. 356, no. 17, pp. 1-94, 1916, DOI). The scan header reads "1916. № 17. ANNALEN DER PHYSIK. VIERTE FOLGE. BAND 51."; a note "ser. 4, vol. 51" is optional. (b) The article continues: p. 94 ends "(Fortsetzung folgt im nächsten Heft.)"; the continuation (III. Teil, Röntgenspektren) is Annalen 356, no. 18, 125-167 (Crossref DOI 10.1002/andp.19163561802). The cited pp. 1-94 contain α, so the page range is correct for this claim. (c) The name "Feinstrukturkonstante" does not appear in the pages read; Sommerfeld calls α "Verhältniszahl", "Fundamentalgröße" and "charakteristische Konstante unserer Feinstrukturen". "Fine-structure constant" is the later name. (d) The .bib key says "Spectral" and the title is German; no problem, noted only.

### Noether1918Invariante (new entry)
- **Authors**: Emmy Noether. **Title**: Invariante Variationsprobleme. **Journal**: Nachrichten von der Königlichen Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen, Mathematisch-physikalische Klasse 1918, Heft 2, 235-257. **DOI**: none.
- **Claim supported**: "the conservation laws behind them are the Noether consequences of time- and space-translation invariance \citep{Noether1918Invariante,Goldstein2002Classical}" (L1315): invariance of the action under translations in time and space gives conservation of energy and momentum.
- **Source URL**: https://de.wikisource.org/wiki/Invariante_Variationsprobleme (per-page transcriptions Seite:InvarianteVariationsprobleme.djvu/1-23, proofread level 4; djvu page N = journal p. 234+N) + https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:InvarianteVariationsprobleme.djvu (scan images of pp. 235 and 255 read visually) + https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0503066 (M. A. Tavel's English translation, LaTeX source read; originally Transport Theory and Statistical Physics 1(3), 183-207 (1971))
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "I. Ist das Integral I invariant gegenüber einer 𝔊_ϱ, so werden ϱ linear-unabhängige Verbindungen der Lagrangeschen Ausdrücke zu Divergenzen — umgekehrt folgt daraus die Invarianz von I gegenüber einer 𝔊_ϱ. Der Satz gilt auch noch im Grenzfall von unendlich vielen Parametern." (§ 1, Satz I, S. 238-239) [translation: "If the integral I is invariant with respect to a 𝔊_ρ, then ρ linearly independent combinations of the Lagrange expressions become divergences — and from this, conversely, invariance of I with respect to a 𝔊_ρ will follow. The theorem holds good even in the limiting case of infinitely many parameters." — Tavel translation, arXiv:physics/0503066, § 1]
  2. "so sagt Satz I im eindimensionalen Fall — wo die Divergenz in ein totales Differential übergeht — die Existenz von ϱ ersten Integralen aus, zwischen denen allerdings nichtlineare Abhängigkeiten bestehen können; im mehrdimensionalen Fall erhält man die neuerdings oft als „Erhaltungssätze“ bezeichneten Divergenzgleichungen" (§ 1, S. 239) [translation: "Theorem I in the one-dimensional case — where the divergence goes over into a total differential — asserts the existence of ρ first integrals, between which, however, non-linear dependencies may subsist; in the multidimensional case, the divergence equations often referred to of late as “laws of conservation” are obtained" — Tavel translation, § 1]
  3. "Mit diesen Zusatz-Bemerkungen enthält Satz I alle in Mechanik u. s. w. bekannten Sätze über erste Integrale" (§ 1, S. 240) [translation: "With these supplementary remarks, Theorem I comprises all theorems on first integrals known to mechanics etc." — Tavel translation, § 1]
  4. "Unter „Verschiebungsgruppe“ sei die endliche Gruppe verstanden: y_i = x_i + ε_i; v_i(y) = u_i(x)" (§ 6, S. 254-255) [translation: "Let “displacement group” be understood to mean the finite y_i = x_i + ε_i; v_i(y) = u_i(x)" — Tavel translation, § 6]
  5. "Die Invarianz gegenüber der Verschiebungsgruppe sagt bekanntlich aus, daß in I = ∫…∫ f(x, u, ∂u/∂x, …) dx die x nicht explizit in f auftreten. Die zugehörigen n Divergenzrelationen Σψ_i ∂u_i/∂x_λ = Div B^(λ) (λ = 1, 2, … n) seien als „Energierelationen“ bezeichnet, da die dem Variationsproblem entsprechenden „Erhaltungssätze“ Div B^(λ) = 0 den „Energiesätzen“, die B^(λ) den „Energiekomponenten“ entsprechen." (§ 6, S. 255; checked against the scan) [translation: "Invariance with respect to the displacement group asserts, as we know, that in I = ∫…∫ f(x, u, ∂u/∂x, …) dx, the x's do not occur explicitly in f. The associated n divergence relationships Σψ_i ∂u_i/∂x_λ = Div B^(λ) (λ = 1, 2, … n) will be referred to as “energy relationships,” since the laws of conservation” Div B^(λ) = 0 corresponding to the variation problem answer to “laws of conservation of energy,” and the B^(λ)'s to the “energy components.”" — Tavel translation, § 6; the missing opening quotation mark before "laws of conservation" is in the arXiv LaTeX]
  6. "Die Energiesätze der klassischen Mechanik und ebenso die der alten „Relativitätstheorie“ (wo Σdx² in sich übergeht), sind „eigentliche“, da hier keine unendlichen Gruppen auftreten." (§ 6, S. 255, footnote) [translation: "The laws of conservation of energy of classical mechanics as well as those of the old “theory of relativity” (where Σdx² goes over into itself) are “proper,” since no infinite groups occur." — Tavel translation, § 6, footnote]
  7. "Invariante Variationsprobleme. (F. Klein zum fünfzigjährigen Doktorjubiläum.) Von Emmy Noether in Göttingen. Vorgelegt von F. Klein in der Sitzung vom 26. Juli 1918" (S. 235, title; checked against the scan) and footer "Kgl. Ges. d. Wiss. Nachrichten. Math.-phys. Klasse. 1918. Heft 2." (S. 235)
- **Claim check**: L1315 SUPPORTED. Theorem I gives one conservation law (a divergence relation) for each parameter of a continuous symmetry group of the action (quotes 1-3). For the displacement group x_i → x_i + ε_i over all n independent variables, which with x = (t, x, y, z) is time and space translation, the n resulting conservation laws are what Noether calls energy theorems with energy components B^(λ) (quotes 4-5), and she identifies them with those of classical mechanics and special relativity (quote 6). Energy from time translation and momentum from space translation is the standard specialization of this passage; the explicit separation into "energy" and "momentum" is carried by the co-cite Goldstein.
- **Status**: VERIFIED (metadata from the scan of S. 235 and the Wikisource transcription; pages 235-257, 23 pages) with primary-source quotes (Wikisource level-4 transcription, two pages checked against the Commons scan) and Tavel's published English translation, marked as such.
- **Flags**: (a) Noether does not use the word momentum ("Impuls") and treats the n translation laws together as "Energiesätze"; the time/space split is the standard reading, not her wording. (b) The translation result is a remark in § 6; the paper's main aim is Theorem II and Hilbert's claim on the failure of proper energy theorems in general relativity. (c) The .bib journal name omits "Königlichen" ("Nachrichten von der Königlichen Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen"; the page footer reads "Kgl. Ges. d. Wiss. Nachrichten"); the shortened form is widely used and acceptable. Optional: add "Heft 2". (d) The title-page footnote reads "Die endgiltige Fassung des Manuskriptes wurde erst Ende September eingereicht." (the final manuscript was submitted only at the end of September 1918). (e) No DOI is known; the .bib has none, which is correct.

### Compton1923Quantum (new entry)
- **Authors**: Arthur H. Compton. **Title**: A Quantum Theory of the Scattering of X-rays by Light Elements. **Journal**: Physical Review (Second Series) 21(5), 483-502 (May 1923). **DOI**: 10.1103/PhysRev.21.483.
- **Claim supported**: "A particle of mass m at rest oscillates at its rest frequency ω0 = mc²/ħ (Eq. (rest_freq)). This is de Broglie's internal clock at the Compton angular frequency \citep{Compton1923Quantum,deBroglie1925Thesis}, the periodic phenomenon from which he derived the matter wave" (L346, after the fix in flag (d)). Compton is cited for the eponym.
- **Source URL**: https://journals.aps.org/pr/pdf/10.1103/PhysRev.21.483 (publisher PDF, freely downloadable; reached from http://link.aps.org/pdf/10.1103/PhysRev.21.483, the location reported by allpapers-locate via OpenAlex and Unpaywall; pp. 483, 484, 487 read visually) + https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1103/PhysRev.21.483 (metadata)
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "The corresponding increase in the wave-length of the scattered beam is λθ − λ0 = (2h/mc) sin² ½θ = 0.0484 sin² ½θ, where h is the Planck constant, m is the mass of the scattering electron, c is the velocity of light, and θ is the angle between the incident and the scattered ray. Hence the increase is independent of the wave-length." (Abstract, p. 483)
  2. "The total energy removed from the primary beam comes out less than that given by the classical Thomson theory in the ratio 1/(1 + 2α), where α = h/mcλ0 = 0.0242/λ0." (Abstract, p. 483)
  3. "α = hν0/mc² = h/mcλ0. (4) Or in terms of wave-length instead of frequency, λθ = λ0 + (2h/mc) sin² ½θ. (5)" (p. 487)
  4. "Second Series May, 1923 Vol. 21, No. 5 ... A QUANTUM THEORY OF THE SCATTERING OF X-RAYS BY LIGHT ELEMENTS By Arthur H. Compton" (p. 483, header and title)
- **Claim check**: L346 SUPPORTED only for the eponym, with a caveat. Compton introduces the length h/mc as the scale of the wavelength shift in scattering (quotes 1, 3) and the ratio α = hν0/mc² of the photon energy to the electron rest energy (quotes 2-3); 0.0242 Å is h/mc for the electron. He does not name a "Compton wavelength", does not give a frequency mc²/h, and says nothing about an internal clock or a periodic process in the particle. The frequency mc²/h = c/(h/mc) is named after him by later usage. The "internal clock" and the matter wave derived from it are de Broglie's, carried by the co-cite deBroglie1925Thesis (not checked in this record). The citation is conventional and acceptable as the source of the name.
- **Status**: VERIFIED (metadata checked against the publisher PDF and Crossref: vol. 21, issue 5, pp. 483-502, issued 1923-05-01) with primary-source quotes read from page images of the publisher PDF.
- **Flags**: (a) The .bib title is in sentence case ("A quantum theory of the scattering of {X}-rays by light elements"); the original is all capitals and Crossref gives "A Quantum Theory of the Scattering of X-rays by Light Elements". This is a style choice, not an error. (b) The PDF's text layer is a noisy OCR (e.g., the running head on p. 502 reads "ARTHUR H. COTTON"); all quotes above were read from the page images, not the text layer. (c) The APS PDF downloaded without authentication (Crossref lists the APS default license); the copy stays in the scratchpad regardless. (d) Suggested rewording of L346 if the attribution is to be exact: "at the Compton frequency mc²/h, the frequency c/λ_C of the Compton wavelength λ_C = h/mc \citep{Compton1923Quantum}, which is de Broglie's internal clock \citep{deBroglie1925Thesis}". Note also that ω0 = mc²/ħ is an angular frequency; the Compton frequency in the ordinary sense is mc²/h = ω0/2π. The sentence equates them only by name, which is common usage. APPLIED 2026-09-22: L346 now says "Compton angular frequency", which matches ω0 = mc²/ħ. The fuller rewording was not applied, because the eponym is all the cite has to carry.

Paper: `SGM/sgm_core_rewrite.tex`. Line numbers are those of the file after the round-1 citation fixes of 2026-09-22; where a record led to a change, the change is marked APPLIED.

  1. "METHODUS INVENIENDI LINEAS CURVAS Maximi Minimive proprietate gaudentes, SIVE SOLUTIO PROBLEMATIS ISOPERIMETRICI LATISSIMO SENSU ACCEPTI. II, §21, p. 42, page image) [translation: "Proposition III. Problem. 21. If Z is a determinate function of x, y and p, so that dZ = M dx + N dy + P dp, to find, among all curves corresponding to the same abscissa, the one in which ∫Z dx is a maximum or minimum." — my rendering]
  3. "unde valor differentialis erit = nν.(Ndx − dP). Quare cum formulæ ∫Zdx valor differentialis nihilo æqualis factus præbeat æquationem pro curva quæsita, hæc erit o = Ndx − dP, vel N − dP/dx = o, qua æquatione natura curvæ quæsitæ exprimetur. Q. E. I." (Cap. II, §21, Solutio, p. 43, page image) [translation: "whence the differential value will be = nν·(N dx − dP). Therefore, since the differential value of the formula ∫Z dx, set equal to zero, gives the equation for the curve sought, this will be 0 = N dx − dP, or N − dP/dx = 0, by which equation the nature of the curve sought is expressed. Which was to be found." — my rendering]
  4. "Æquatio hæc igitur semper erit differentialis secundi gradus, nisi in P plane non insit p. Nam si p continetur in P, tum in dP inerit dp; quod ob p = dy/dx differentialia secundi gradus involvet." (Cap. II, §21, Coroll. II, p. 44, page image) [translation: "This equation will therefore always be a differential equation of the second order, unless p is entirely absent from P. Lagrange (1788) supplies the mechanical form with generalized coordinates. SUPPORTED.

### DAlembert1743Traite
- **Authors**: Jean le Rond d'Alembert. **Title**: Traité de dynamique, dans lequel les loix de l'equilibre & du mouvement des corps sont réduites au plus petit nombre possible, & démontrées d'une manière nouvelle, & où l'on donne un principe général pour trouver le mouvement de plusieurs corps qui agissent les uns sur les autres, d'une manière quelconque. **Publisher**: David l'aîné, Paris (1743).
- **Claim supported**: L548, "which is d'Alembert's principle: on the realized path the gravitational force and the inertial reaction sum to zero \citep{DAlembert1743Traite,Lagrange1788Mecanique,Goldstein2002Classical}." L2110, "That is d'Alembert's principle, the vanishing of the sum of the applied and inertial forces \citep{DAlembert1743Traite,Goldstein2002Classical}, read as a condition on a frequency field."
- **Source URL**: https://archive.org/details/b30530593 (Wellcome Collection scan of the 1743 first edition; title page from the OCR, Seconde Partie pp. 49-51 read from rendered page images).
- **Verbatim quote(s)**:
  1. "TRAITÉ DE DYNAMIQUE, DANS LEQUEL LES LOIX DE L'EQUILIBRE & du Mouvement des Corps sont réduites au plus petit nombre possible, & démontrées d'une manière nouvelle, & où l'on donne un Principe général pour trouver le Mouvement de plusieurs Corps qui agissent les uns sur les autres, d'une manière quelconque. Par M. d'Alembert, de l'Académie Royale des Sciences. A PARIS, Chez David l'aîné, Libraire, rue Saint Jacques, à la Plume d'or. MDCCXLIII." (title page, OCR text)
  2. "Les Corps n'agissent les uns sur les autres que de trois manières différentes qui nous soient connues : ou par impulsion immédiate, comme dans le choc ordinaire, ou par le moyen de quelque Corps interposé entr'eux, & auquel ils sont attachés, ou enfin par une vertu d'attraction réciproque, comme font dans le système Newtonien le Soleil & les Planetes. Les effets de cette dernière espece d'action ayant été suffisamment examinés, je me bornerai à traiter ici du Mouvement des Corps qui se choquent d'une manière quelconque, ou de ceux qui se tirent par des fils ou des verges inflexibles." (Seconde Partie, Chap. I "Exposition du Principe", p. 49, page image) [translation: "Bodies act on one another in only three different ways known to us: by immediate impulse, as in ordinary collision; by means of some body placed between them to which they are attached; or finally by a power of mutual attraction, as the Sun and the planets do in the Newtonian system. The effects of this last kind of action having been sufficiently examined, I shall confine myself here to the motion of bodies that collide in any manner, or of those that pull one another by threads or inflexible rods." — my rendering]
  3. "DÉFINITION. J'appellerai dans la suite Mouvement d'un Corps, la vitesse de ce même Corps considerée en ayant égard à sa direction, & par quantité de Mouvement, j'entendrai à l'ordinaire le produit de la masse par la vitesse." (p. 50, page image) [translation: "Definition. I shall hereafter call the motion of a body the velocity of that body considered with regard to its direction, and by quantity of motion I shall mean, as usual, the product of the mass and the velocity." — my rendering]
  4. "PROBLÊME GENERAL. 50. Soit donné un système de Corps disposés les uns par rapport aux autres d'une manière quelconque ; & supposons qu'on imprime à chacun de ces Corps un Mouvement particulier, qu'il ne puisse suivre à cause de l'action des autres Corps, trouver le Mouvement que chaque Corps doit prendre." (p. 50, page image) [translation: "General problem. 50. Given a system of bodies arranged in any manner relative to one another, and supposing that a particular motion is impressed on each of these bodies which it cannot follow because of the action of the other bodies, to find the motion that each body must take." — my rendering]
  5. "Delà résulte le Principe suivant, pour trouver le Mouvement de plusieurs Corps qui agissent les uns sur les autres. Décomposés les Mouvemens a, b, c &c. imprimés à chaque Corps, chacun en deux autres a, α; b, ϐ; c, x; &c. qui soient tels, que si l'on n'eût imprimé aux Corps que les Mouvemens a, b, c &c. ils eussent pû conserver ces Mouvemens sans se nuire réciproquement ; & que si on ne leur eût imprimé que les Mouvemens α, ϐ, x, &c. le système fût demeuré en repos ; il est clair que a, b, c seront les Mouvemens que ces Corps prendront en vertu de leur action. Ce Q. F. Trouver." (p. 51, page image; the first a, b, c are italic in the print and denote the impressed motions, the second a, b, c are roman and denote the motions actually taken; the third lost motion is printed as an italic x) [translation: "From this follows the following principle for finding the motion of several bodies acting on one another. Decompose the motions a, b, c, etc. impressed on each body each into two others, a, α; b, β; c, x; etc., such that if only the motions a, b, c, etc. had been impressed on the bodies, they could have kept these motions without hindering one another, and that if only the motions α, β, x, etc. had been impressed on them, the system would have remained at rest; it is clear that a, b, c will be the motions these bodies take by virtue of their action. Which was to be found." — my rendering]
  6. "Donc les Mouvemens α, ϐ, x &c. doivent être tels qu'ils ne dérangent rien dans les Mouvemens a, b, c &c. c'est-à-dire, que si les Corps n'avoient reçu que les Mouvemens α, ϐ, x &c. ces Mouvemens auroient dû se détruire mutuellement, & le système demeurer en repos." (p. 51, page image) [translation: "Therefore the motions α, β, x, etc. must be such that they disturb nothing in the motions a, b, c, etc.; that is, if the bodies had received only the motions α, β, x, etc., these motions would have had to destroy one another and the system remain at rest." — my rendering]
- **Claim check**: The paper states the principle as "applied plus inertial force sum to zero". That is the standard modern textbook form: Lanczos writes it as F + I = 0 with the inertial force I = −ma, and Goldstein as the virtual-work statement Σ(F^(a) − ṗ)·δr = 0. Both descend from Lagrange's reformulation in the Méchanique analitique (1788). D'Alembert's own 1743 principle is different in wording and in scope. It is a statement about motions (velocities with direction), not forces: the impressed motion of each body is split into the motion it actually takes and a "lost" motion, and the lost motions must be in equilibrium (quotes 5 and 6). He applies it to bodies in collision or linked by threads and rods, and explicitly sets aside bodies acting by mutual attraction, which is the case the paper uses it for (quote 2). For a single free particle the principle has no content beyond Newton's second law. So the attribution of the name is standard and the 1743 citation is a correct historical source for the principle's origin. The form the paper uses is Lagrange's and the textbooks', carried here by Goldstein. SUPPORTED as the standard attribution, with the flag below.
- **Status**: VERIFIED for the quotes (page images). Claim: SUPPORTED WITH FLAG.
- **Flags**: (a) Recommend the text say "d'Alembert's principle in its Lagrangian form" or add Lagrange1788Mecanique beside Goldstein, and keep the 1743 citation as the historical origin; the 1743 text neither uses force language nor covers gravitation (quote 2). (b) At L548 the "force" in the sum is gravitational; d'Alembert's text excludes attraction explicitly. This is a point a historically minded referee would raise. APPLIED 2026-09-22 to flags (a) and (b): Lagrange1788Mecanique now sits between the 1743 source and Goldstein at L548, so the force form the sentence uses has its own source. L2110 is unchanged, because it states the principle in general and does not apply it to gravitation. (c) Metadata: place, publisher and year match the title page. The bib title is the standard short title of a longer title (quote 1); acceptable. (d) The Greek β in quotes 5-6 is printed as the variant ϐ; transcribed as printed.
